title: API keys and test mode

scenes.say: The Sentinel API lets your own systems run checks without anyone opening the dashboard. In this video, you'll create a test key, learn what test mode does, and send your first AML screening.

show.subtitle: Sentinel by DeepTrack · Developer quick start

scenes.say: Click API Keys in the menu on the left, under Developer. Keys are shown by their prefix only. Admins and Developers can create, rotate and revoke them. Everyone else can only look.

show.highlight: case:Keys are shown by prefix only

scenes.say: Click New key. Give it a name that describes the integration, such as Core banking onboarding.
Next, choose the environment. Test gives sandbox results, with no charges. Live runs real checks, and they're billed. New keys start on Test, and you can't change it later, so create one key of each.
Scopes decide what the key can call. Untick Everything to choose only what this integration needs. For a first call, Run AML screenings and Read check results are enough.
Then you'd click Create key. Sentinel shows the full key once, and stores only a hash, so copy it straight into your secrets manager. We'll cancel here.
Keep the key out of your code. Read it from an environment variable, and send it on every request as a bearer token, with a JSON content type.

show.subtitle: Content-Type: application/json · every path starts with /v1/

scenes.say: Your first call is an AML screening. Post to slash v1 slash verify slash aml. Only the subject's name and entity type are required. The Help chapter has the same call in curl, Node and Python.

show.scroll: case:needs the Run AML screenings scope

scenes.say: With a test key, the check is finished at once: completed, pass, and sandbox true. No lists are screened, nothing is charged, and the names you send are not stored. With a live key, the status is queued. Keep the id to fetch the result.
To replace a key, click Rotate. You get a new key straight away, and the old one keeps working for 24 hours while you deploy. To stop a key at once, click Revoke.

Each key has a per-minute limit set by your plan. Business allows 500 requests a minute. If you hit a limit, you get a 429 with a Retry-After header. A 401 means the key is wrong or revoked, and a 403 usually means a missing scope.
That's your first key and your first call. To learn more, open chapter C1 in Help, Quick start.
